title: Contact
metaTitle: Contact Us About Your Oil Mineral Rights
metaDescription: Get in touch to ask questions about selling your oil mineral rights or royalty interest, or to request a no-obligation offer. One point of contact, no pressure.
heroLead: You can ask a question without requesting an offer, and you can request an offer without committing to anything. Both are fine reasons to reach out.
intro: Whether you have a specific question about a royalty statement, want to understand how a division order works before you sign one, or you're ready to talk about a specific interest, reach out and you'll hear back from one point of contact rather than a rotating queue.
There's no pressure attached to a first conversation. Plenty of owners reach out just to understand the process before they're ready to decide anything, and that's a completely normal way to start.

sections.heading: What to have ready, if you have it
paragraphs: It helps to know roughly which county and state your minerals are in, and whether the interest is currently producing, but none of that is required to reach out. If you have a deed, division order, or recent statement handy, mentioning it speeds things up, but don't wait to gather documents before saying hello.

sections.heading: What happens after you reach out
paragraphs: We'll ask a few basic questions about your interest and, if you're interested in an offer, what documents you can share. If you're just asking questions, we'll answer them directly, there's no script pushing every conversation toward a sale. You set the pace from there.

sections.heading: Response time
paragraphs: We aim to respond within a few business days of hearing from you, typically faster. If your situation is time-sensitive, say so when you reach out and we'll prioritize accordingly.

sections.heading: If you're contacting us on behalf of a family member
paragraphs: It's common for one person in a family to handle inquiries on behalf of siblings or an aging parent who co-own an interest together. That's fine, just let us know upfront who else is involved and what your role is, since any eventual closing will need each owner's own signature on their portion, even if one person is coordinating the conversation.

If the interest passed through an estate that's still being settled, mention that too, it doesn't stop the conversation from starting, but it does affect the documentation the title team will eventually need.

sections.heading: Other ways to prepare before reaching out
paragraphs: If you'd like a head start, our resources library covers how to read a royalty statement, what a division order confirms, and the documents typically needed to sell. None of it is required reading before you contact us, but some owners find it useful to skim beforehand so the first conversation covers more ground.

sections.heading: If you're comparing us against another buyer
paragraphs: Bring the other offer with you when you reach out, and we'll be direct about whether we can be competitive with it, without asking you to disclose numbers you'd rather keep private. Comparing two offers works best when both are pricing the same wells and the same decimal interest, so we'll ask a few clarifying questions to make sure that comparison is a fair one before saying anything about our own number.
We're not going to pressure you to drop a conversation with another buyer, and if the other offer is genuinely stronger, we'd rather tell you that than waste your time.

sections.heading: If your question isn't about selling at all
paragraphs: Not every question we get is about a sale. Owners sometimes reach out with a question about a confusing royalty statement, a division order they're unsure about signing, or a general question about how decline works on a specific well. We're glad to answer those too, even if you're not currently considering an offer, since a clearer understanding of your own interest is useful regardless of what you eventually decide to do with it.

faqs.question: Do I have to be ready to sell to contact you?
faqs.answer: No, plenty of people reach out just to ask questions or understand the process, and there's no pressure to move toward an offer until you're genuinely ready to have that fuller conversation with us.

faqs.question: What information should I include when I reach out?
faqs.answer: The state and county where your minerals are located and whether the interest is producing are helpful, but a brief description is enough to start the conversation, and we'll ask follow-up questions as needed to fill in the rest.

faqs.question: Will I keep talking to the same person throughout?
faqs.answer: Yes, we keep contact to one point of contact through the process rather than routing you through a rotating call center, from your very first question all the way through closing.

faqs.question: Can I ask a general question about my royalty statement?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, general questions about statements, division orders, or how title works are welcome even if you're not currently considering a sale, and there's no obligation attached to asking, now or later.

faqs.question: How quickly will I hear back?
faqs.answer: Typically within a few business days, and sooner if you let us know your situation is time-sensitive, since we'd rather prioritize accurately than make you wait unnecessarily on a simple question.
